task: Fix the duplicate job execution after the distributed lock TTL was set too short.

candidate_memories.content: Jobs are executing twice because the distributed lock expires before the job finishes on slow execution paths.
The distributed lock TTL must be extended from 30 seconds to 5 minutes to cover the maximum job duration.
The 30-second TTL was set for a fast code path; slow paths (large data sets) can take up to 4 minutes.
Duplicate executions only happen for jobs processing data sets larger than 100,000 records.
Session 2 note: the job monitoring dashboard shows duplicate execution counts for large data set jobs.
Distributed job locks are implemented using Redis SETNX with automatic expiry.
Session 7 note: the job scheduler was upgraded to use leader election for single-run guarantees.
Old practice: distributed locks used a 10-second TTL before job execution times were profiled.
The job executor uses a goroutine pool with a maximum concurrency of 20.
Session 3 note: the monitoring team added a duplicate execution counter to the job metrics dashboard.
Old lock guide: the 30-second TTL was chosen to balance lock holder failure detection and execution time.
Distributed lock TTLs must exceed the p99 execution time of the longest expected job execution.
Session 11 note: the data team found that monthly reconciliation jobs take up to 6 minutes.
Redis lock keys use a random nonce to ensure only the original lock holder can release the lock.
A job execution analysis in session 8 showed p50 job times of 15 seconds and p99 of 3.5 minutes.
The job scheduler retries failed jobs up to 3 times before sending to the dead-letter queue.
Extend distributed lock TTLs with heartbeat renewal for jobs that can run longer than the initial TTL.
Session 5 note: the platform team added a job execution time histogram to the monitoring suite.
Old job guide: the lock TTL was set to match the job timeout, which was incorrectly set to 30 seconds.
Job results are stored in the job_results table with the execution duration recorded.
